Sorry, I totally didn't mean to come across that way. I'm a PC guy myself, I'm just not very familiar with pricing trends here, since I only got into PC gaming a few months ago.

That truly is the crux of it. The physical copies absolutely must be sold. Not only has the money gone into the packaging, discs, manuals etc, the games also take up a physical space in warehouses and on store shelves, and when you are looking at a triple A title that can mean millions of physical copies.

It is better for the consumer of course when companies take a more digital angle and allow reduced rates for something that really only costs in bandwidth and power once the game is ready to launch, but any developer still releasing on physical media is losing more money the longer those physical copies sit so they rarely take that approach. As the titles age they have to be reduced, and are overshadowed by newer, flasher games to the point they frequently wind up selling at cost or below.
Yet it's better to wait some months so you can play the finished game, instead of betatesting.

It happens when a company consider their game "a classic" (which Inquisition is not). Distant Worlds (not a RPG) is like 4 years old still price of 60€.
